model_annotation: The top portion of Figure 3 displays a line plot illustrating the performance of five different large language models (LLMs) — Base, MEND, FT, IKE, and ROME — across varying co-occurrence numbers of biomedical knowledge, as measured by the size of the set |D(s, o)|. The x-axis represents the co-occurrence number, labeled as “|D(s, o)|”, and is presented on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^0 to 10^4, with tick marks at regular powers of ten. The y-axis represents performance in percentage (%), ranging from 55% to 65%, with tick marks at 55, 60, and 65. The plot contains five lines, each corresponding to a different model: Base (black solid line with circle markers), MEND (green solid line with square markers), FT (blue dashed line with triangle markers), IKE (red dashed line with diamond markers), and ROME (purple dashed line with star markers). The Base model shows a consistent decline in performance from approximately 64% at 10^0 to around 58% at 10^4. The MEND model exhibits a steady increase, starting at about 59% and rising to approximately 64% at 10^4. The FT model remains relatively flat, hovering around 57% across the entire range. The IKE model starts at about 58% and gradually declines to roughly 57%. The ROME model begins at approximately 57% and shows a slight upward trend, ending near 59%. The bottom portion of Figure 3, not shown in this image, is described in the text as showing the distribution of triples across different co-occurrence groups, highlighting the long-tail nature of biomedical knowledge. The overall plot demonstrates that model performance varies significantly with co-occurrence frequency, with some models (like MEND) improving on rare knowledge and others (like Base) performing better on more common knowledge.
